chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Ays ibn al-Qasim who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Can the man and the woman perform ghusl from one vessel?' He said: 'Yes, they should pour [water] onto their hands before placing their hands in the vessel.'

He said: And I asked him about the residue of the menstruating woman, so he said: 'Do not perform wudu from it; but you may perform wudu from the residue of the sexually impure woman when she is trustworthy, then she washes her hands before entering them into the vessel.'
And it was so that the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) used to perform ghusl, he and Aisha, from one vessel, and they would both bathe together.

key_terms.الْجُنُب: A person in the state of major ritual impurity (janaba), e.g. after sexual intercourse
key_terms.الْحَائِض: A woman in the state of menstruation (hayd), whose leftover water is ruled impure
key_terms.سُؤْر: Residue water left in a vessel after drinking or use — relevant for determining ritual purity
key_terms.مَأْمُونَة: Trustworthy/reliable — a condition for permissibility of using her leftover water
key_terms.يُفْرِغَانِ: They both pour out [water onto their hands] — the prescribed manner before dipping into a shared vessel

ai.seo_question: Can a man and woman perform ghusl from the same vessel in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issues a series of rulings on sharing bathing water. A man and woman may perform ghusl from one vessel provided they rinse their hands over the vessel first before dipping them in. The residue of a menstruating woman may not be used for wudu, but the residue of a sexually impure woman (junub) may be used if she is trustworthy and rinses her hands first. The Imam cites the practice of the Prophet (SAWW) bathing with Aisha from one vessel as a precedent for shared bathing.
